text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.5% today, extending a broader two-week rally as crude oil climbed back above $104 per barrel following Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's key pipeline infrastructure. The outage has tightened global oil supply—analysts warn that if the pipeline stays offline beyond five to seven days, inventories could tighten sharply and push prices higher. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices typically compress margins in the short run, but the real driver here appears to be market conviction that a supply crunch is coming, which boosts the value of refining capacity itself.

The refining sector is running at 97.8% capacity utilization, leaving almost no slack to absorb further supply disruptions. Combined with the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran-backed militants attacking Saudi infrastructure while Iranian officials negotiate with China—the market is pricing in sustained tightness and upside risk to energy prices, which shifts investor focus away from margin pressure and toward supply-side leverage.
